title: World's top drivers to compete for season titles at Abu Dhabi Desert Challenge
Antonelli quickest in Las Vegas GP Qualifying as Verstappen inherits pole position
article_text:
Kimi Antonelli set the fastest time in Qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, but will start sixth after a grid penalty.

Kimi Antonelli finished fastest in Qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, but Max Verstappen will inherit pole position as the Mercedes driver serves a grid penalty.

World Champion Antonelli jumped to the top of the times with a 1m 33.893s on his final effort, leaving the Italian 0.258s clear of Verstappen.

But Antonelli will serve a five-place grid penalty due to power unit changes, meaning he will start P6 as Verstappen is set to start from pole.

The Dutchman will be joined on the front row by Mercedes driver George Russell, with Lando Norris (McLaren) and Isack Hadjar (Red Bull) on the second row.

Arvid Lindblad finished sixth quickest followed by Oscar Piastri, with the McLaren driver set to serve a 10-place grid penalty.

Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls) and the two Alpines of Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto completed the top 10.

Ferrari suffered a difficult day, as both Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton failed to reach Q3 after the pair finished P11 and P12 respectively during the second part of Qualifying.

They were joined on the sidelines by Nico Hulkenberg's Audi, the Williams of Carlos Sainz – who will serve a 10-place grid penalty for power unit changes – Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi) and the second Williams of Alex Albon.

Formula 1 rookie Rafael Camara just missed out on reaching Q2 by less than one-tenth to Bortoleto, the Haas driver having suffered a spin at the start of Q1.

Also knocked out was Sergio Perez's Cadillac, the Aston Martins of Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll, as well as the second Cadillac of Valtteri Bottas.

Ollie Bearman was P22, the Briton having helped tow Haas team mate Camara and not setting a representative lap time with a grid penalty set to be served due to power unit changes.

With only one dry session under their belts after a washout on Thursday, drivers and teams entered Qualifying with limited data and ventured out onto a circuit with a track temperature of just 15C for the opening 18-minute segment.

With all cars fitted with the soft Pirelli tyre as drivers headed out except Bortoleto's Audi, which remained in the garage initially with an issue.

Camara also had problems, suffering a huge spin at Turn 1 after locking his rear brakes before rejoining unharmed, as drivers conducted several laps to generate heat in the tyres.

Russell, who had topped a wet FP2 and dry FP3, initially topped the times with a 1m 35.580s before Verstappen posted a 1m 35.276s, with team mate Hadjar slotting into second.

Times continued to tumble, Norris setting a 1m 35.109s which was quickly beaten by Leclerc's 1m 35.040s, with both McLaren and Ferrari attempting to choreograph slipstreaming between their respective drivers down The Strip.

Antonelli briefly went fastest with a tow from Russell, before Russell became the first driver to dip below the 1m 35s barrier with a 1m 34.664s, which remained quickest at the chequered flag.

Antonelli improved to within 0.020s of his team mate, as Leclerc was best of the rest from Norris, Verstappen and Hadjar, as Lindblad, Lawson, Piastri and Sainz completed the top 10.

Formula 1 rookie Camara just missed out on reaching Q2 by less than one-tenth to Bortoleto, the Haas driver having been given a tow by team mate Bearman on his final attempt.

Also knocked out was Perez's Cadillac, the Aston Martins of Alonso and Stroll, the second Cadillac of Bottas and Bearman, the Briton not setting a representative lap time with a grid penalty set to be served due to power unit changes.

Even before the cars hit the track for Q2 there was drama, with Lindblad noted for an unsafe pit release as the Racing Bulls driver pulled into the path of Albon's Williams, with the incident set to be investigated after the session.

Lindblad's team mate began to catch the eye, jumping to the top of the times with a 1m 35.048s, which was beaten by Piastri's 1m 34.966s, the McLaren driver remaining fastest after the initial runs.

Hamilton, meanwhile, was left in P13 and reporting a lack of grip having run off the track at Turn 1, with the Briton also struggling to find a tow which was proving crucial throughout the field.

Russell soon moved back to the top of the field with a 1m 34.617s, while Hamilton jumped up to P8 initially but was quickly put back into the elimination zone as other drivers improved, notably Hadjar, Lindblad and the two Alpines of Gasly and Colapinto.

Verstappen finished fastest with a 1m 34.394s, just over one-tenth ahead of Gasly, with Russell, Piastri, Norris, Lindblad, Colapinto, Lawson, Hadjar and Antonelli completing the top 10.

Leclerc, who ran deep on a quick lap, failed to progress by just over one-tenth, with Hamilton half a second away from making it through to Q3. Also failing to advance was Hulkenberg, Sainz, Bortoleto and Albon.

After the initial runs in Q3, Verstappen sat top of the times with a 1m 34.151s, the Red Bull driver benefitting from a tow down the back straight which left him nearly two-tenths clear of Norris.

Russell sat third from Hadjar, the Mercedes driver telling his race engineer he needed a better track position, having not benefited from a tow.

Such was the benefit of the tow that the Mercedes, Alpines and Racing Bulls drivers jostled for position on their out laps, with Antonelli only just making it onto his final flying lap.

title: REVERSE GRID RACE: Alba Larsen charges from ninth to claim second victory of 2026 in Las Vegas
article_text:
Alba Larsen claimed her second F1 ACADEMY victory with a remarkable recovery from ninth on the grid in Las Vegas, holding off 2026 Champion Alisha Palmowski in a dramatic Reverse Grid Race.

The Ferrari driver seized the lead after an eventful opening five laps and resisted Palmowski’s late challenge following two Safety Car interruptions, setting a new record for the lowest winning grid position. Megan Bruce completed the podium in third to strengthen Campos Racing’s position in the Teams’ title fight.

It was Mathilda Paatz who started from Reverse Grid pole ahead of Ella Lloyd and Natalia Granada, but Lloyd made the better getaway into Turn 1. Paatz reclaimed the lead at the following corner as Nina Gademan joined the fight, passing Lloyd for second while Palmowski climbed from sixth to fourth.

Larsen was also making rapid progress after starting P9 following a three-place grid penalty, overtaking Palmowski on Lap 2 before a lock-up for Lloyd promoted both drivers further up the order.

The battle for the lead intensified on Lap 3 as Paatz, Gademan and Granada went three-wide. Contact from Granada into the side of Gademan sent the Alpine driver into path of Paatz. The subsequent contact eliminated Paatz, while the Sephora driver emerged ahead but was subsequently handed a five-second time penalty for her involvement in the collision.

The Safety Car was deployed to recover Paatz’s car, with Gademan later forced to pit for a front-wing repair after receiving the black-and-orange flag.

Granada retained the lead at the restart, but a costly lock-up sent the Sephora driver wide and allowed Larsen to take the lead on Lap 5, completing her charge from ninth to first. Palmowski soon followed into second, setting up another battle between the pair.

However, a second Safety Car interrupted proceedings on Lap 6 after Lisa Billard was eliminated in an incident involving Rachel Robertson and Luna Fluxa Cross. Robertson and Emma Felbermayr also retired following contact in a separate incident.

Larsen maintained her advantage when racing resumed on Lap 9, but Palmowski immediately applied pressure, setting a succession of quick laps as she closed on the Ferrari driver.

Behind them, Bruce remained close to Granada in the battle for third, with the Sephora driver’s five-second penalty set to drop her down the order. The Campos driver eventually made her move on the final lap, taking third position on track.

Despite Palmowski’s late charge, Larsen responded with the fastest opening sector on the last lap and held on to secure her second consecutive Reverse Grid Race victory. Palmowski recorded the fastest lap of the race with a 2:07.917 on her final tour but was unable to find a way past the Dane.

Palmowski crossed the line second ahead of Bruce, with Jade Jacquet taking fourth after a late overtake on Ella Stevens, who secured her best result of the season in fifth.

Rafaela Ferreira finished sixth ahead of Payton Westcott, while Granada dropped to eighth following her penalty, the last of the points-paying positions.

With Palmowski, Bruce and Ferreira all scoring points, Campos Racing now hold a 52-point advantage over MP Motorsport as they look to secure their first F1 ACADEMY Teams’ title.

One final race remains before the curtain falls on the 2026 F1 ACADEMY season. With the Teams’ title and second place in the Drivers’ Standings still up for grabs, Palmowski will lead the field from pole position for one last showdown under the Las Vegas lights. The Feature Race gets underway on Sunday at 16:20 local time (UTC−8).

title: Shohei Ohtani Secures Career-Long Sponsorship With New Balance
article_text:
[Sports Chosun Reporter Na Yu-ri] Shohei Ohtani has been promised sponsorship until the day he retires from his playing career.

On November 20 (Korean time), the U.S. fashion magazine 'GQ' reported, "Ohtani has signed a historic extension with New Balance."

According to the report, Ohtani agreed to extend his sponsorship contract with long-time partner New Balance, a sports brand, until his retirement from active play. 'GQ' reported, "Japanese baseball icon Ohtani has made a groundbreaking deal, extending his sponsorship with a long-time partner until the end of his baseball career, adding a new chapter to his achievements. While only a handful of athletes, such as LeBron James and Cristiano Ronaldo (both Nike), and Damian Lillard (Adidas), have secured lifetime sponsorships, Ohtani’s deal is the first to cover an entire playing career and the first such case in Major League Baseball."

In an interview with 'GQ', Ohtani said, "I have great trust in the brand. Of course, we’ve built a good relationship. They’ve listened well to my requests, which requires significant trust. Our relationship has been really good and smooth so far. There was no hesitation in extending the contract."

New Balance, which will sponsor Ohtani until his retirement, has decided to rename its in-house research lab. Originally named the "Sports Research Lab," it will now be called the "Shohei Ohtani Sports Research Lab."

Ohtani recently visited the Boston headquarters to analyze spikes for the next season. Ohtani recorded a disappointing performance this season due to injuries to his left knee and right biceps. He revealed, "There were moments this year when my heel slipped upon landing during pitching." Consequently, the spikes he will wear next season are expected to address these issues.

As the only two-way player in Major League Baseball, Ohtani does not change his shoes when switching between pitching and batting, wearing the same spikes for both.

In the 'GQ' interview, when asked what advice and encouragement he would give to children who want to be like him, Ohtani said, "If you want to succeed, baseball is a sport that requires a lot of repetitive practice. You must consistently build on the fundamentals. Once you reach a certain level, baseball becomes really, really difficult. At that point, you should reconsider why you play baseball. Is it because you love the sport? If you have that passion and love, you can overcome tough times."

Reporter Na Yu-ri youll@sportschosun.com

title: NFL reportedly wants new rights deals in place by start of next season
article_text:
The timeline is accelerating for the NFL’s expedited media rights negotiations.

John Ourand of Puck reported Thursday that the NFL is now believed to want its new media rights deals completed before the new season begins in September, earlier than the fall timeframe that had been previously reported. The league is expected to negotiate and announce its new deals one-by-one, starting with Paramount and then Fox, Ourand wrote, with all of them taking effect immediately.

Technically, the NFL does not have the ability to exit its current media rights deals until after the 2029 season at the earliest (2030 for ESPN), but there is little expectation that any of the league’s partners will oppose the expedited talks. According to Ourand, it is believed that the new contracts will run through the 2033 or 2034 seasons, meaning that the existing rightsholders can lock up NFL rights for the next seven or eight years by agreeing to the early talks. Currently, the networks are guaranteed only four additional seasons if they choose to wait for the league’s contractual opt-out.

But the early talks are likely to come with some sacrifices, and not just the obvious financial ones. The NFL is expected to use the opening created by the negotiations to carve out inventory for new packages. NFL EVP/media distribution Hans Schroeder told Alex Sherman of CNBC last month that the league plans to engage not just its existing partners in its upcoming talks, but additional suitors who are on the outside looking in. Schroeder: “We’re going to listen and probably have a lot of different people that want to have that want to have a conversation with us.”

The league is already believed to be shopping the four game windows that were freed up as part of its now-completed sale of NFL Network to ESPN, with Austin Karp and Ben Fischer of Sports Business Journal reporting last week that YouTube is among the frontrunners for that package.

The incumbent rights partners are likely to end up in the position of paying more for less, but given the ability to guarantee that they will remain in the NFL business into the middle of the next decade, it is unlikely that any will turn up their nose at the chance.

title: NIKE extends sponsorship with Bank of America Chicago Marathon through 2036!
article_text:
NIKE extends sponsorship with Bank of America Chicago Marathon through 2036!

Editor’s note: The Bank of America Chicago Marathon is one of the world’s most important marathons. As NIKE works to convince the retail community, investors and the consumer that “Running is in NIKE’s DNA” (a quote from former NIKE CEO Mark Parker), extending the contract with the Bank of America Chicago Distance Series (Shamrock Shuffle 8k, Chicago 13.1 miles, Bank of America Chicago Marathon) is a huge testament to the importance of the Windy City in NIKE’s plans to resurrect the running business of NIKE. Please note that NIKE’s renewed vigor in running has taken much reflection, and as with any evolution, there are challenges and pain.

Over the last week, NIKE had announced several new launches in the performance running category, most of which will be offered in 2027. It was a whirlwind of launches, perhaps too many in such a short time. The astonishing speed was, in my observance, part of the story: NIKE needs to show that it is overly enthusiastic about running.

In 2026, NIKE built nearly two weeks of events with local retailers around the Bank of America Chicago Marathon. NIKE also built events around the recent NYC marathon (event not sponsored by NIKE). In the weeks before NYC, NIKE also ran major race promotions in both LA and London.

Now that NIKE has had the proverbial fire lit under its backside, social media, especially Instagram, abounds with content on SWOOSH TC athletes, NIKE global running events, NIKE running product launches, and Elliott Hill, NIKE CEO, visiting the world to rebuild NIKE’s business in China and reputation around the world; one wonders who will be left at home in Beaverton and the new HQ in New Delhi to actually do the work needed for these plans to succeed. One other point needs to be made: Instagram seems to be the tool that NIKE uses to communicate, yet many of its customers and, more importantly, potential customers are not on that platform, or any platform for that matter. It is the challenge of communicating in a post-literate world with Balkanized running cultures.

NIKE has to build consistently great products, support brick-and-mortar retailers, placate big retailers, and convince consumers that the brand remains relevant in their recreational lives.

Extending the contract between NIKE and the Bank of America Chicago Marathon is one of the brand’s smartest sports marketing decisions. It is also a no-brainer. Big, high-profile running events deepen NIKE’s relationship with runners, who want more than a pair of fast running shoes.

What I find amusing is that most brands, including NIKE, rely heavily a influencers and the ever-changing Instagram algorithm.

Here’s my issue: Sixty thousand marathoners will begin training shortly for the 2027 Bank of America Chicago marathon, to be held on October 10, 2027. Those miles are personal, and for NIKE to have credibility, it has to rely on coaches, experts, and yes, influencers who actually know the sport. For the most part, NIKE does that; for the most part, NIKE is building some incredible performance running product.

Brands need to realize that while they romanticize elite and sub-elite marathoners, the average time at NYC was 4 hours, 43 minutes. The average time of the 54,500 finishers in Chicago 2026 was 4 hours, 30.03-4 hours, 30.04 minutes.

Years ago, former NIKE CEO Mark Parker related a story about a lunch with the late Apple wunderkind, Steve Jobs.

Products that you lust after. But you also make a lot of crap. Just get rid of the crappy stuff and focus on the good stuff.”

In my mind, good stuff extends to running events. In extending their sponsorship of the Bank of America Chicago Marathon, NIKE is protecting the “good stuff.

Well done, NIKE. Just remember, you have to breathe while running.

CHICAGO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Today, the Bank of America Chicago Marathon announced the extension of its partnership with Nike through 2036, continuing a relationship that has connected Nike with runners in Chicago since 2008. The partnership spans the full Bank of America Chicago Distance Series, including the Chicago Marathon, Shamrock Shuffle and Chicago 13.1, creating more opportunities for runners to train, race and progress through Nike’s growing World of Race.

“For nearly two decades, our partnership with Nike has helped shape the experience of every runner who crosses our start lines,” said Carey Pinkowski, executive race director, Bank of America Chicago Marathon. “This extended partnership gives participants access to the latest Nike training tools, innovative apparel and footwear. As we look ahead, we’re excited to work together to continue pushing the boundaries of what’s possible for runners in Chicago and around the world.”

The extended partnership reflects a shared belief in the power of running to bring people together through experiences that celebrate runners, strengthen community and build excitement around the sport. That belief has guided Nike for more than 50 years, inspiring the brand to serve runners of every pace and distance as they pursue their goals and discover what’s possible.

“As a World Major, Chicago is one of those moments on the running calendar that the whole sport looks forward to, bringing together the fastest athletes in the world and everyday runners on the same streets,” said Tanya Hvizdak, VP and General Manager, Nike Running. “We’re incredibly proud to extend this partnership and continue showing up for runners across their entire journey, while working together to move the sport forward for years to come.”

title: Hollywood, a $60m team valuation and the fast-growing world of SailGP
article_text:
What do the likes of Ryan Reynolds, Hugh Jackman, Anne Hathaway, Deontay Wilder, Sebastian Vettel and Kylian Mbappe have in common? They are all investors in SailGP, one of the fastest growing and adrenaline fuelled sports in the world.

In the seven years since its inception, the league has attracted a notably diverse and eclectic ownership base – sovereign wealth funds, celebrity investors, Formula One drivers, and institutional asset managers among them.

The most recent signal of that interest came earlier this year when American Magic team acquired the Danish team Rockwool for $60m, the highest reported valuation in league history. Five years ago, SailGP sold teams for between $5m and $10m.

The next wave of expansion is expected to push values toward $75m. That trajectory – roughly a tenfold increase in franchise value in under five years – is the kind of return profile that institutional capital finds extremely attractive.

Backed by sports investor and Orlando Magic co-owner Doug DeVos, the purchase of Rockwool underlined SailGP teams’ status as premium properties commanding serious capital.

The Danish team had previously been league-owned; its sale marks another step in SailGP’s shift toward a predominantly private ownership model.

Devos is the son of the co-founder of Amway, the American direct selling giant and a hugely successful businessman in his own right. He is a passionate sailor having spent his childhood sailing on the Great Lakes against his siblings. He loves sport, both as a hobby and as a vehicle for investment.

Sir Russell Coutts, the co-founder of SailGP with Larry Ellison, did not envisage such star pulling power in the early days. But the leverage and profile that such stars can generate, combined with the business acumen of individuals such as Devos, has meant that the sport’s growth and appeal have been turbocharged.

In an interview with The Athletic last year, Coutts said: “What you want is a Ryan Reynolds who’s going to come in and add his marketing flair to the team.

“Connecting a name with a team has value but you’re really looking to have them adding value to the team on an ongoing basis.

“Ryan is a marketing genius. He’s got a great sense of humour, and you can see what he’s done with his other sports entities (such as Wrexham FC).”

Devos backed the American Magic team representing the New York Yacht Club in the 2021 and 2024 America’s Cup. He has sailed competitively throughout his life.

“It's an amazingly complex sport, and that's why I love it,” he says. “When I was younger in the US, I played American football and I always loved that; the team aspect, offence, defence, special teams. You have all these elements, and you have got to bring people together. And I think sailing has that.

“You have the team on the water, you have the team off the water, you're sailing against all these other boats in a variety of conditions, and the conditions always change. The wind, the sea state, you know, the position on the racecourse. It's an ongoing mix of variables that are just incredibly challenging. It keeps me coming back!

“We have to be attractive to people who are not sailors and who see this competition for the challenge and the excitement that it can bring. And then you bring the sport to people on the shore.”

Devos and his son know, and have often sailed with, Nicolai Sehested the Danish driver. So when Devos got serious about coming on board with SailGP, the Danish boat was one of the teams that the league still owned and was available.

“As things started going down the track it, I said, ‘Boy, this could be the team for us and we’re having a ball'.”

So, was the purchase an indulgence or a demonstration of his faith in the value of SailGP and its direction of travel?

“Obviously it's a bit of both, because I'm passionate about sailing. I can't disregard that. But one of the things that we have really learnt, is that there has to be a commercial connection to this sport,” Devos said.

“We learnt that in basketball. We've been involved with the Orlando Magic, our family has, for 35 years now. So, we've been able to watch the NBA develop. You watch it over the history of the NBA or any professional leagues in the US, where it starts with just passion, then someone has to figure out how to have a commercial connection and reach an audience and make it work.

“We saw the commercial connection that SailGP was developing. We shared that vision to develop an audience, to develop a connection with people who weren't sailors, who loved racing and who could present the sport in a new attractive way.

“We’ve been watching SailGP since the beginning. Getting involved was very much a business decision. With that you have a partnership of people coming together, under the leadership of Larry and Russell. They had a really clear vision and we wanted to be part of it.

Devos is clear about where he sees SailGP in five to 10 years’ time.

“I think it can be more powerful. I think we can attract a few more teams and I think we can get to having teams who are not only an efficient operation but a very effective attraction, and you build a following that that isn't just showing up because they're in town, you now start following the team. We can build that attractiveness, we can build the brands with our commercial sponsors and with the teams and with the athletes, and you can start to build that following.

title: F1 Las Vegas GP: Russell fastest in final practice after Verstappen collision
article_text:
George Russell collided with Max Verstappen in a tense third practice session at the Las Vegas Grand Prix as the Mercedes Formula 1 driver topped the timesheets.

After both of Thursday's practice sessions had been derailed by rain, the Las Vegas Strip was buzzing with activity at dusk on Friday. The sole remaining practice session became crucial as it presented the only dry running heading into qualifying and the race, as all 22 cars sprinted out of the pitlane in short order.

Amid chilly 14C temperatures, the Thursday rainfall only made the 6.2km circuit around the Las Vegas Strip even more difficult to drive, with surface grip extremely limited.

Verstappen survived a sideways scare and steering rack issues to lead the early running with a 1m35.675s on soft tyres, by far the most popular tyre in cold conditions as it was easier to fire up to temperature.

Just after the halfway mark Russell took over top spot with a 1m35.124s, the Briton aiming to finish the season on a high as he declined a Mercedes turbo upgrade to avoid a grid penalty. Russell further lowered his own benchmark to a 1m34.805s lap, before becoming one of several cars to find the runoff area on the slippery circuit.

The urgency to get plenty of clean laps in was on full display with Verstappen and Franco Colapinto almost coming to blows in their quest for clean air. Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar also lobbied for a penalty for Williams' Alex Albon.

Annoyed by Verstappen forcing his way past, Lando Norris couldn't hide his glee when the four-time world champion subsequently locked up and sailed into the runoff area. "Instant karma, amazing," he said over team radio.

The biggest clash followed right at the end of the session, again involving Verstappen, as he tried a similar move on Russell on the straight. Undeterred, Russell sent his Mercedes down the inside of Turn 14 to re-pass the Red Bull, making side-on contact as he muscled Verstappen off the track. The incident will be investigated by the FIA’s stewards. "Fun and games," Russell described the incident on the radio.

Norris initially came closest to overhauling Russell in the closing minutes of the session, settling for second with a 1m35.060s lap. Russell found late improvements too, though, to pull out a massive seven-tenth lead on Norris at the top of the timesheets with laps of 1m34.306s and 1m34.041s.

Norris was demoted to third by his world championship heir Kimi Antonelli, while Charles Leclerc skated his way to fourth after sampling several escape areas.

Ahead of Verstappen, Colapinto was fifth for Alpine on a circuit that should suit the Enstone team's slippery car, as evidenced by the Pierre Gasly's shock pole back in Monza.

Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson was seventh, followed by Lewis Hamilton, Gasly and Arvid Lindblad.

title: ATP Ventures unveiled, men’s top tour significantly increasing prize money
article_text:
The board of men's tennis' top-tier ATP has given the green light to launch ATP Ventures, a new vehicle set to manage the body's commercial and media rights.

This comes as part of a wider sweep of changes to the structure of men's top-tier tennis that will also see the total prize money available to players increase to over $350 million by 2028. That figure is currently set at $270 million.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

It also forms the latest chapter in OneVision, the long-term campaign to increase the ATP's revenue and commercial appeal that began in 2023 (having been in development since 2020).

The creation of ATP Ventures will bring all of the media and sponsorship rights for the ATP Tour under one roof for the first time.

It comes with plans to create a joint commercial venture between the ATP and women's tennis' WTA, which had fallen through earlier this year.

The launch of this new vehicle has been unanimously approved by the ATP's board, alongside the shareholders of the ATP Media wing.

It comes as the end-of-year ATP Finals take place currently in Turin, Italy.

The rights combined will cover those held by the ATP Tour itself, ATP Media, as well as those held by the Tennis Data Innovations vehicle.

The Florida-based ATP has said that work on the agreement will begin next year, and that the venture will become operational from the start of 2028.

Andrea Gaudenzi, chair of the ATP, commented: "The next phase of OneVision strengthens our product, while ATP Ventures will transform how we take it to market. Bringing ATP Media, TDI and our central sponsorship business together under one aligned commercial strategy gives us a huge opportunity to grow the Tour, tell a stronger story around our players and bring fans closer to the sport.”

Regarding the financial element of this news, the increased player prize money will include an increase in the bonus pool figure to $50 million, a bonus of $25 million covering end-of-year rankings, and $26 million in player pension funding.

As a contrast, the 2026 bonus pool for ATP professionals only comes to $21 million.

The ATP Tour announced earlier this month that central partnership revenues had increased 49% year-on-year in 2026, to more than $100 million, for the first time.

This came on the back of new agreements and expanded investments from long-standing partners including flag carrier airline Emirates, tech company Infosys, parts manufacturer Nitto, luxury carmaker Lexus, home appliances corporation Haier, and tyre manufacturer Yokohama.

Overall, OneVision represents the organization's long-term strategic plan to reform professional tennis, align interests between players and tournaments, and grow the sport’s commercial digital footprint.

Earlier this year, the tour re-elected Gaudenzi as chairman for a third term until 2028, meanwhile.

Recent growth has also been driven by the launch of the ATP’s dedicated Licensing and Retail team within its central business division in 2025, which has opened the door to new licensing agreements, including K-Swiss’ agreement to create a collection of five ATP-branded tennis shoes.

title: Apollo scraps $2bn loan to Man City owners; Hull partner with Corpay
article_text:
The Apollo Sports Capital investment firm has reportedly pulled the plug on a potential $2 billion loan to City Football Group (CFG), the parent company of English soccer giants Manchester City and 12 other clubs, despite the two parties reaching the final stages of negotiations.

According to the Financial Times (FT), the financing was intended to provide additional liquidity for the ownership group and to refinance its existing credit facilities, but Apollo ended the talks after Manchester City were recently found guilty of significant financial breaches.

The FT report stated that Companies House filings show that club owner Sheikh Mansour instead injected £100 million of equity into CFG through his Newton Investment and Development vehicle in the month after an independent commission published its findings in September.

The commission found Manchester City guilty of 114 of 115 financial breach charges laid by the top-flight Premier League and revealed that the club artificially inflated its organic revenue by over £900 million ($1.19 billion) across nine years.

A 40-page report contains details of how the Manchester club – which won three Premier League titles during the nine years these financial breaches took place, between 2009 and 2018 – concocted 'sham' sponsorship deals with commercial partners to inflate its organic revenue and thus not fall foul of the league's Financial Fair Play (FFP) rules.

City filed inaccurate accounts for every single season during this time period – if these had been filed properly, the club would have broken league spending limits significantly, as well as those set down by European soccer's governing body UEFA.

Essentially, City used owner funding from its Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) ownership vehicle to top up and boost the value of sponsorship deals signed with Abu Dhabi-based partners between 2009 and 2018. As the commission put it, the club was "relying on sham agreements to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs."

In total, the club recorded £949.9 million in sponsorship income across the nine seasons in question – the commission found that only £119.2 million of this actually came from sponsors, with the other £830.6 million simply provided by the club owners instead.

Man City continues to protest its innocence and lodged an appeal in early October, which will be heard in mid-December.

A rule introduced by the Premier League in the summer requires appeal hearings to conclude within 12 weeks and decisions to follow within 30 days, although that timeframe can be set aside if necessary.

Should City's appeal fail, the commission has wide-ranging powers to impose sanctions ranging from fines and points deductions to expulsion from the league.

The collapse of the loan deal with Apollo reflects the uncertainty surrounding the outcome of City's appeal and the sanctions that could follow should it prove unsuccessful when a judgment is delivered in the new year.

The private equity group launched its Apollo Sports Capital branch in 2025 and has already acquired a major sports team in the European market, taking a majority stake in Spanish soccer's Atletico Madrid last year.

Recently, the firm also agreed a major $2.6 billion financing deal with the New York Yankees, the iconic Major League Baseball (MLB) franchise, that includes an equity stake in the team.

Earlier this year, Apollo also led a $225 million investment into Major League Pickleball and the PPA Tour, the two largest professional organizations for the US-based racket sport.

Through a multi-year agreement, the company will become the club’s official foreign exchange (FX) partner.

As part of the deal, Corpay Cross Border will deliver FX risk management solutions to support Hull’s day-to-day business operations. In addition, its platform will enable the club to manage global payments through a single point of access.

The partnership comes just a month after Corpay announced a deal with Newcastle United.

Over the past few years, Corpay has become a prominent sports sponsor across several major markets, with a particularly strong presence in soccer.

The US-based company has tie-ups with fellow English Premier League sides Manchester City and Everton, Spanish giants Real Madrid, Italian Serie A heavyweights AC Milan, US outfit Atlanta United, and Major League Soccer.

In its return to the Premier League for the first time since the 2016-17 season, Hull is currently 13th with 11 points.

title: Toto Wolff wants answers after George Russell misses Vegas pole despite “ideal” final-lap position
article_text:
Toto Wolff wants answers after George Russell misses Las Vegas GP pole by 0.073s to Max Verstappen despite ideal track position

For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

Mercedes left Friday night qualifying at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit with the fastest car on track, yet team principal Toto Wolff still had questions to answer. World champion Kimi Antonelli topped Q3 with a 1m33.893s, only to drop to sixth on the grid due to a five-place penalty for taking Mercedes’ updated ADUO turbocharger. Instead of team-mate George Russell inheriting pole, Red Bull’s Max Verstappen snatched top spot with a 1m34.151s - edging Russell’s 1m34.224s by just 0.073 seconds.

The result stung after Russell had looked untouchable earlier in the evening, topping final practice with a 1m34.041s that put him 0.911s clear of Antonelli. Complicating matters in Q3, Russell had asked Mercedes for a slipstream from his already-penalised team-mate.

Instead, a messy final out-lap left Antonelli trailing the pack, allowing the Italian to pull a tow worth up to 16 km/h down the Strip straight from cars ahead—including Russell.

Asked after qualifying whether Mercedes should have orchestrated a better tow to aid Russell’s fight for second in the Drivers’ Championship, Wolff dismissed track positioning as the culprit.

"Actually, George for me had the perfect position. He was four seconds behind the car in front," Wolff said. "We need to find out because I think there was some kind of Turn 7, 8, 9 - whether there was a mistake or something else happened, I don’t know, to be honest, but it looked like the ideal position for a pole lap because he was quickest all the time."

Even without pole, Russell lines up second alongside Verstappen on Saturday night with major championship stakes on the line. Sitting third in the standings and 17 points behind Verstappen, Russell has a prime chance to make serious ground after both Ferraris - Charles Leclerc (11th) and Lewis Hamilton (12th) - were knocked out in Q2.

Tension between the front-row rivals is already running hot. Late in FP3, Verstappen and Russell tangled wheel-to-wheel at Turn 14 after Verstappen passed the Mercedes and slowed into the corner, prompting the Dutchman to complain over team radio that Russell had "pushed me into the barrier". Following a post-session review, the FIA stewards handed Verstappen a warning for the skirmish.

Asked what he expected when the pair launch side by side toward Turn 1, Wolff didn't downplay the prospect of fireworks.

"Well, with cinema, if they try to go through the first corners together, we shall be watching," Wolff said.

title: Cadillac CEO Towriss on Herta’s future and Bottas’ extension
article_text:
With Cadillac opting to retain Valtteri Bottas for 2027 rather than promoting Colton Herta, CEO Dan Towriss has explained what the next steps might be for the American driver.

Cadillac CEO Dan Towriss has given an update on Colton Herta’s future after the American missed out on a potential F1 promotion in 2027, following the announcement that Valtteri Bottas will remain with the squad.

While Sergio Perez’s contract extension was confirmed ahead of the Mexico City Grand Prix in October, speculation persisted over whether Bottas would stay in the other seat or if Herta – who has acted as a test driver for the team this year – might be given the opportunity.

Alongside embarking on his debut F2 campaign in 2026, Herta has participated in six Free Practice 1 outings for Cadillac – meaning that he accumulated enough Super Licence points to allow him to race in F1.

However, the American outfit ultimately decided to retain Bottas for 2027, a decision that Towriss reiterated was “right” for them as he spoke to the media on Thursday at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

When asked if there was ever any doubt over Bottas’ position, Towriss responded: “We did want to take a look at it. I think as we look across the races, while [his pace in] practice and Qualifying was similar to Checo, race pace was down.

“Some of that [involves] things behind the scenes that are out of Valtteri's control. We did want to take a look at that. We were working hard to get Colton Herta ready as well.

“It's important to have an American driver for our team with our team, racing, but ultimately, when we took a look at it, Valtteri's the right guy.

“We want to keep Checo and Valtteri together, their experience, the continuity, what they bring to the team. Ultimately it was the right decision for the team and we were happy to extend Valtteri. He's been absolutely fantastic for us.”

In terms of what this means for Herta’s next steps, Towriss explained that there are “a number of options on the table” for the 26-year-old.

“We've offered him a reserve position,” the American said. “The seat's open for ’28, so there are options on the table for Colton. There are options in other sports as well. I think he's decided on a direction, but we're still in conversations on that and look forward to seeing what Colton wants to do.”

Towriss acknowledged that Herta was “disappointed” by the decision and went on to praise the former IndyCar racer for taking on the challenge of the past year.

“It was definitely a tough decision – a tough discussion with Colton,” he explained. “I think he was disappointed. There was a lot of work, a lot of a build-up [to] go into this. I know Colton was very brave in even taking on this risk, going into F2 and trying to cram all this learning in.

“I think it was obvious it was a very tough season for Colton in F2 this year, but I think the work that he did in FP1s and the TPC [Testing of Previous Cars] setting [was] quite strong and showed that he really is capable of driving this car. But when we look at where the team is right now and what's needed for the team, Valtteri was the best decision going forward.

“But we're going to continue to talk to Colton about the options that are on the table and give it a little bit of time, because I think he is disappointed to not have that opportunity. So much went into this, but he's just a tremendous talent and we're excited about what's ahead for him.”

title: Frontier Airlines & BarkleyOKRP ink the world’s first-ever official sports NIL butt sponsorship
article_text:
November, 2026.- Most airlines launch premium seats with typical luxury marketing and visuals. Not Frontier Airlines. They decided to pen the world’s first-ever official sports NIL butt sponsorship, literally sponsoring the actual rear ends of college football’s heaviest players.

Frontier and BarkleyOKRP partnered with two #2-ranked University of Georgia offensive linemen, Jahzare Jackson (6’10”, 350 lbs) and Juan Gaston (6’7”, 360 lbs), for what they’re calling the world’s “biggest” NIL deal. And they took the signing quite literally. The 710-pound duo made their endorsements official by dipping their backsides in paint and stamping their contracts with their butts.

The campaign comes as Frontier works to reshape perceptions of the airline, introducing a series of cabin enhancements that include First Class seating, more extra-legroom options, in-seat power and Starlink Wi-Fi. Rather than relying on traditional premium airline advertising, BarkleyOKRP turned an NIL partnership into an unexpected demonstration of one of those upgrades: If Frontier’s new First Class seats can comfortably accommodate two SEC offensive linemen, they can accommodate just about anyone.

The campaign launches November 18 across social and digital channels, bringing an unexpected twist to both airline advertising and the increasingly crowded world of NIL deals.

title: Chairwoman of Bundestag's Sports Committee to QNA: Qatar Enhanced its Status as a Global Sports Hub
article_text:
Berlin, November 20 (QNA) - Chairwoman of the Committee on Sports and Volunteering of the German Bundestag Aydan Ozoguz, who is also a Member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, affirmed that the State of Qatar has demonstrated its ability to host major sporting events of global significance, praising the efforts made over recent years to establish the country as a global sports hub.

In exclusive remarks to Qatar News Agency (QNA), Ozoguz said that Qatar's hosting of the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022 had demonstrated its ability to provide the organisational requirements, infrastructure and extensive technical capabilities necessary to stage a sporting event of such magnitude and global importance.

She stressed that there was considerable scope for expanding Qatari-German cooperation in sports, the exchange of expertise, the development of young talent, volunteering and parliamentary diplomacy. Ozoguz added that the State of Qatar had made significant efforts over recent years to strengthen its presence on the international sporting stage, noting that one aspect deserving particular attention was how to make long-term use of the expertise gained from organising major sporting tournaments and events.

The Chairwoman of the Bundestag's Committee on Sports and Volunteering noted that the sports facilities, training centres and sports medicine facilities developed by Qatar offered opportunities and benefits extending beyond the hosting of individual international events, as these facilities would continue to serve sports and society, particularly young people, on a sustainable basis.

Ozoguz outlined several areas of potential cooperation between Qatar and Germany in the sporting field, highlighting opportunities to benefit from Germany's contributions and expertise in the sports club system, the development of emerging talent and support for athletes pursuing dual careers that combine sporting activities with education or vocational training.

She also pointed to Germany's experience in organising grassroots and elite sports, stressing the importance of mutual support between the two countries in achieving their shared objectives.

Regarding the role of sports in strengthening Qatari-German relations, the Bundestag committee chairwoman affirmed that sports possessed a unique ability to bring people closer together and transcend geographical, linguistic, cultural and even political boundaries.

She noted that sporting activities created opportunities for people to meet and communicate beyond the traditional frameworks of political and economic relations. She also noted that sports constituted an important pillar of relations between Qatar and Germany, not only at the level of official institutions but also among male and female athletes and the peoples of both countries. She added that sports could help strengthen existing connections between sporting federations, clubs, universities and non-governmental organisations, opening broader avenues for institutional and community-level cooperation.

She also emphasised the role of Qatari-German cooperation in creating greater opportunities for young people in both countries to participate in joint programmes and initiatives, considering that open exchanges among young people could help build trust and enhance mutual understanding among all parties.

Regarding the prospects for international cooperation and the exchange of expertise, Ozoguz said that her participation in parliamentary discussions with international sports organisations and federations had reinforced her conviction that sporting issues could no longer be addressed in isolation from political developments and international relations.

She said that the belief that sports and politics could be completely separated did not reflect reality, as the two fields were interconnected in numerous ways. She added that constructive and positive cooperation between countries could reduce the likelihood of this interaction between politics and sports producing negative consequences or developments that could damage the reputation of sports.

The Chairwoman of the Committee on Sports and Volunteering of the German Bundestag, explained in remarks to Qatar News Agency (QNA) that organising sporting events, supporting male and female athletes, and developing modern facilities could no longer be viewed from a purely national perspective, making international cooperation and the exchange of knowledge and expertise indispensable.

She affirmed that Qatar and Germany had opportunities to expand their cooperation in this field, both at the level of sports policies and through the exchange of expertise and knowledge among sports federations and organising committees of major tournaments and events.

Ozoguz expressed her hope for intensified communication and exchanges between the two countries' parliamentarians, universities and sports federations, allowing both sides to benefit from each other's experiences and expertise.

Regarding volunteering, Ozoguz told QNA that voluntary work constituted one of the fundamental pillars of German society, noting that approximately 27 million people in Germany participated in volunteer activities, representing around 37 percent of the population aged 14 and above.

She proposed several ideas for Qatari-German cooperation in volunteering, including the possibility of developing joint programmes for young people and volunteers in both countries, enabling them to meet and exchange experiences through participation in sporting events, club activities and social projects. She added that such initiatives could provide direct opportunities for interaction among young people and strengthen human and community ties between the two countries.

Ozoguz added that volunteering encompassed a wide range of activities, including disaster protection, sports club activities, childcare and youth support, sports coaching and refereeing, and participation in organising activities and managing the day-to-day operations of clubs.

She stressed that without the contributions of these volunteers, German sports would not have achieved their current breadth and diversity. She affirmed that appreciation for voluntary work should not be limited to verbal praise but should be accompanied by appropriate organisational conditions, reduced bureaucratic procedures while maintaining necessary oversight, sustained support and greater public recognition of the value of volunteer contributions. She noted that individuals who assumed voluntary responsibilities deserved appropriate recognition and appreciation from society for their efforts.

title: Duka: The sponsorship law is a step forward that must bring real support for sport
article_text:
We welcome and endorse the government’s proposal for the draft law “On Donations and Sponsorships”. We thank the ministry responsible for sport for its efforts, the initiating MPs and all members of the parliamentary committee, from both political sides, for the generally favorable positions expressed during the discussion. Support for sport requires this spirit of cooperation.

For at least ten years, the football community and the FSHF have sought a fundamental change in the way sponsorships are encouraged. We have submitted concrete proposals and maintained continuous dialogue with the institutions. The draft law is a step forward, but to bring real financing and development, it needs several important improvements.

This request is also supported by the contribution that football makes to Albania’s budget and economy. In 2025 alone, the FSHF and its members paid 342,400,806 lek in taxes and contributions.

Football also brings financing from abroad, creates employment and activity for Albanian businesses. The UEFA GROW SROI study, based on 2020 data, estimated the economic, social and health benefits of participation in football at around 46 million euros per year. Considering that at that time we had 18,587 registered footballers; today that number is 25,000, the economic, social and health benefits reach 70 million euros per year.

Therefore, support for football should be seen as an investment that creates value for the economy and society. We ask that part of this contribution be returned for its development, for children, for academies, for clubs and for sports infrastructure.

First, sponsorship should be clearly defined as an alternative payment of profit tax.

Within the 30% level and legal limits, the amount a business directs to sponsorship should be recognized as a settled tax obligation. The legal wording should be clear, so that businesses have certainty about how their contribution is treated.

Second, the overall fund should be larger, increase every year and guarantee support for football.

The proposed ceiling of 2 billion lek for art, culture and all sport is restrictive for the needs of these sectors.

We ask that the total annual value of sponsorships benefiting from this mechanism be no less than 10 billion lek. The law should provide for a mandatory mechanism for increasing this value every year, in line with economic growth and tax revenue growth, guaranteeing that it does not decrease.

Within this amount, we ask for a guaranteed quota for football, with a clear and transparent allocation for the Federation, clubs by category and academies.

We must ensure that small clubs and academies also benefit from this mechanism. Their sponsorship is an investment in young people and in the national teams of the future.

Third, the relationship between business and sport should function without prior approvals for each contract.

Eligibility criteria should be defined in the law. Football activity that meets these criteria should be recognized as an activity of public interest, without the need to prove this for each sponsorship.

Transparency should be guaranteed through registration, documentation and financial and legal control after the sponsorship is carried out, with clear sanctions for violators. This gives businesses certainty and beneficiaries responsibility.

Finally, part of the funds should be guaranteed for sports infrastructure.

Pitches and training facilities are our greatest need and the basis for increasing participation. Investments in them serve communities and remain for future generations. And these cannot be achieved with the proposed limit of 2 billion per year, but should be provided for no less than 10 billion per year.

These proposals aim to make the initiative functional, predictable and controllable. As the FSHF, we are ready to continue cooperation with the government, the Parliament and all interested actors, so that this opportunity translates into more children in sport, more stable clubs and better infrastructure throughout Albania.
